name: Offline Cheap Text LLM Gemma 3
tagline: EXPERIMENTAL, and SLOW — minutes per answer, not seconds. Google's Gemma 3, running entirely on your device.
description:
⚠ EXPERIMENTAL — PLEASE READ THIS BEFORE YOU INSTALL

This is a technology demonstration, not an everyday assistant. It exists to prove that a real language model can ship inside a GIF, run sealed in the sandbox, and answer with nothing whatever leaving your device. Judged as a chat assistant, its speed is NOT ACCEPTABLE for common use — and it is not trying to be. Install it to watch the thing work, not to get work done.

HOW SLOW, CONCRETELY. The engine runs SINGLE-THREADED in the browser: GitHub Pages cannot send the COOP/COEP headers that would let it use more than one core, so the model writes at about the pace of slow typing. Measured on a phone, an offline provider of this kind took 362 seconds — six minutes — to answer a single ordinary question. This one is at the faster end of that range, which still means minutes. On a desktop it is better, and still far slower than any hosted model you have used. The FIRST answer of a session is slower again, because it loads the weights before writing a word.

WHAT IT COSTS BEFORE IT SAYS ANYTHING: a 769 MB download, kept on this device.

WHAT YOU GET FOR THAT: privacy that is structural rather than promised. No account, no key, no network path at all — not "we don't look", but "there is nowhere for it to go". If that is what you came for, it is worth the wait. If you want a fast, capable assistant, leave this uninstalled and point Settings → AI models → Cheapest text LLM at a hosted endpoint instead; every app that asks for cheap text will use that, and answer in seconds.

———

Offline Cheap Text LLM Gemma 3 is a PROVIDER app: install it, keep it in your Providers folder, and assign it to Cheapest text LLM in Settings → AI models. From then on, every app that asks the computer for cheap text — Ask AI, Chat drafts, game hints — is answered on this device. No account, no key, nothing leaves your machine.

The engine is llama.cpp compiled to WebAssembly (wllama, MIT), sealed in the GifOS sandbox with zero network access. The brain is Google's Gemma 3 1B Instruct, 4-bit quantized — downloaded once at install (~769 MB, hash-verified by GifOS) and cached on this computer.

It is a SMALL model by the standards of this kind of app — ~769 MB — which matters a lot because the engine runs single-threaded in the browser: a bigger brain is a slower one, answer for answer. Pick it when you want the quickest answers this approach can give.

A built-in few-MB self-test model proves the whole pipeline instantly (clearly labeled — it speaks token soup, not answers) while the real weights download.

Note on licensing: the ENGINE is MIT, but the Gemma WEIGHTS are not open-source-licensed — they are governed by Google's Gemma Terms of Use, which carry use restrictions that follow the model. GifOS does not host or redistribute them; they are downloaded from Hugging Face on your own device.
license: MIT (app + engine); weights under the Gemma Terms of Use
